A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RawMed study. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on MIMIC-IV, eICU and MIMIC-IV-ED, including fidelity, clinical utility, privacy, component ablations and scalability results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds conditional-generation experiments and measurements of postprocessing modification and rejection rates.

M1.justification: Appendix F.4 adds conditional generation by prepending age, gender and admission attributes during autoregressive training and supplying them during generation, optionally with initial real events. This is a limited procedural extension; the compression architecture and temporal model remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The three datasets remain unchanged. Appendix F.4 adds conditional trajectory generation and continuation scenarios on MIMIC-IV and eICU, evaluated through prediction of age, gender and admission attributes from generated events.

E2.justification: SDV, RC-TGAN and ClavaDDPM remain in the corresponding ICU and emergency-department comparisons, and adapted RealTabFormer remains in the six-hour compression comparison. Table 17 evaluates RawMed conditioning variants against a real-data reference without introducing another external baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 changes the I-PCC exclusion threshold from fewer than 0.1% of records to fewer than 100 records, without establishing that experiments were rerun. New conditional evaluations exclude static prefixes from classifier inputs, bin age, restrict admission diagnoses to four organ-system categories, and compare static-only conditioning with an initial quarter of real events.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds an error analysis measuring event modifications and event/patient rejection at both postprocessing stages. Appendix F.4 tests the effect of adding initial medical context to static conditioning. Existing quantization, temporal-component and observation-window analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting in Tables 4 and 11–13 is unchanged. The added conditional results and rejection rates provide point estimates without new run counts, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Existing table values are retained. New Table 17 reports conditional AUROCs, including eICU age scores of 0.65 with static-only conditioning and 0.69 with initial events. Appendix D.2 newly reports patient rejection rates reaching 16.90% for eICU and 54.53% for MIMIC-IV during column-specific validation.

T1.justification: Quantization equations, the autoregressive objective, feature-count definitions and metric formulas are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical theorems or proofs. The revised I-PCC inclusion threshold changes evaluation filtering rather than mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies 'minimal preprocessing' as 'minimal lossy preprocessing,' and the introduction correspondingly focuses its criticism on information-losing transformations. The principal claims about multi-table EHR generation, the evaluation framework and comparative performance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains how individual event errors produce high patient rejection, particularly for long trajectories, and argues for complete postprocessing. Appendix F.4 attributes perfect MIMIC-IV gender prediction to gender-specific laboratory reference ranges and discusses weaker eICU gender performance. Section 7 nevertheless retains its earlier treatment of conditional generation as future work.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 now explicitly represents patient grouping, temporary tables and valid-event counts, documenting patient-level rejection already described in v1's prose. Appendix F.4 supplies conditioning and evaluation construction details. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware descriptions and repository access information remain.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 adds Cho et al. on CNN encoding of raw EHRs to contextualize compression of textual representations. The additional Theodorou et al. bibliography entry duplicates an already cited work; other reference renumbering and bibliographic corrections do not substantially change research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, refines preprocessing terminology, corrects the related-work double negative, expands Appendix D.2 and adds Appendix F.4. The main scientific narrative and section organization otherwise remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 17, expands and relocates Algorithm 1, and reflows appendix tables around the added material. Existing figures and table structures are substantially retained; the revision does not constitute a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The rejection-rate analysis makes previously unquantified filtering costs visible, while Appendix F.4 adds useful evidence about conditional generation and explains a gender-prediction shortcut. Expanded pseudocode also improves documentation. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by Section 7 still describing conditional generation as future work and the unexplained I-PCC threshold revision accompanying unchanged scores.
